subject: Medicine
title: Acute Ischemic Stroke: Recognition, Imaging and Reperfusion Decisions
preview: Stroke treatment depends on last-known-well time, neurological disability, vessel status and imaging—not one memorized number.

sections.title: First actions
points: Activate a stroke system of care and assess whether symptoms are disabling.
Do not dismiss posterior circulation symptoms such as ataxia or diplopia simply because classic face-arm-speech findings are absent.

sections.title: Use the right treatment pathway
points: Intravenous thrombolysis is time-dependent in eligible patients; selected extended-window and mechanical thrombectomy strategies use additional clinical and imaging criteria.
Blood pressure and antithrombotic decisions depend on treatment pathway and contraindications.

sections.title: Exam trap
points: Do not assume a normal early CT rules out ischemic stroke.
Do not substitute antiplatelet treatment for eligible reperfusion therapy.

quickRevision: Recognize sudden focal deficits; assess airway, glucose, neurological findings and last-known-well time.
Noncontrast brain imaging is used urgently to assess for hemorrhage and guide reperfusion decisions.
Eligibility for thrombolysis or thrombectomy depends on clinical and imaging selection under current pathways.
